new_statements.translation: [...tones] In the present state of our knowledge of the language we could only retain the hypothesis that three tones exist in Kajakse, namely high (´), mid, not marked graphically here, and low (`). Examples: sin 'tooth', sún 'think', fàn 'mouth', fúká 'dog', liisi 'tongue', ʔàbàr 'blood', sigàr 'long', fársò 'horse' ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kajakse is treated as a tone language with (provisionally) three level tones, high, mid and low; the sketch makes no statement about word stress or accent placement (no occurrence of 'accent' in the Kajakse pages by in-volume search).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the three-tone analysis itself is flagged by the author as a hypothesis ('l'hypothèse de l'existence de trois tons')
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation forms (isolated nouns/verbs); nothing on word- or phrase-level stress. Absence of a stress statement verified only by keyword search of the Google Books preview (queries accent, 'accent tonique', tonème), not by reading the full chapter.
new_statements.identity_note: Alio 2004 describes 'kajakse d'Am-Dam' (Am Dam, Sila/Ouaddaï, eastern Chad) = Kajakse/Kadjakse [ckq], kaja1254; the SIL survey wordlist is from Amtalaté village (Canton Kadjakse). No dialect subdivision is reported by either source.
